name: Bell 214
summary: A heavy Bell utility helicopter derived from the Huey: a single-engine BigLifter and a larger twin-engine Super Transport, used for logging, firefighting and offshore work.

wings: Very wide-chord two-blade main rotor on both versions
No stabilizer bar above the rotor head, unlike a Huey
engines: Single turbine with one large exhaust duct on the older version; twin exhausts on the larger twin
Big engine hump on the roof
fuselage: Big boxy Huey-like cabin with large sliding doors
Skids on tall legs; the twin is bulkier and longer
tail: Tall boom with a large vertical fin and a two-blade tail rotor

tellTales: Oversized Huey-like body with no stabilizer bar above the rotor head
Very wide-chord two-blade rotor over a big engine hump
One large exhaust duct on the roof, or a bulkier twin-exhaust version, on skids

confusedWith.howToTell: A Huey has a stabilizer bar above the head and a slimmer body; the 214 has wide-chord blades with no bar and a bigger engine hump.
The 412 is smaller and rounder with a four-blade rotor; the 214 keeps a two-blade rotor and is larger and bulkier.
The 222/430 have a sleek swept nose and smooth cowling; the 214 is a boxy utility machine.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
